newsitem.title: GERMANY: Krupp, Thyssen sign steel pact.
newsitem.headline: Krupp, Thyssen sign steel pact.

text.p: German steel companies Krupp Hoesch and Thyssen AG said late on Wednesday that they had signed a basic agreement of understanding on founding a joint steel-producing company.
The firms said in a joint statement that Thyssen would take a 60 percent stake in the new firm while Krupp would take a 40 percent share.
The statement said the accord avoided forced layoffs and was the best possible solution to ensure the future of the city of Dortmund as an industrial centre.
The two companies said they were confident that the new venture would create a market-leading steel firm.
